demos.title: App shell
demos.description: The chrome around every signed-in screen. It renders an already-resolved nav and owns no nav logic: a Sider at desktop width, a hamburger sheet below it, decided by @stapel/core's useBreakpoint — which now answers on the FIRST client render, so the phone branch is never painted on a desktop and swapped out a frame later. The admin section is the one a pair hangs a staff screen from and nobody declares; it is synthesised, LISTED for everyone, and switched off with its reason beside it when the staff capability is absent, because an entry that vanishes teaches nobody the screen exists.

variants.description: Desktop: sidebar, nested submenu, routed content.
The admin section, listed and closed, with the reason under it.
Phone: the chrome collapses to a header and a hamburger.
The same phone chrome with the nav sheet open.

demos.title: Public shell
demos.description: A storefront's chrome, and a sibling of AppShell rather than a flag on it: top bar, browse bar, measured content, footer — and never a Sider. On a phone the browse bar collapses into a sheet while the header and its search box stay, because a storefront whose search disappears on a phone is a storefront nobody searches. Omit accountSlot and a sign-in link renders anyway: the absence of a sign-in button on a public page is not clean, it is a dead end for the one person the page exists to convert.

variants.description: Desktop: brand, search, browse bar, and the default sign-in CTA.
A host's own account menu steps in for the CTA.
No nav and no categories: no hamburger onto an empty sheet.
Phone: the header and its search stay; browse collapses.

demos.title: Theme mode control
demos.description: Sun, moon, half-disc — a real ARIA radio group: one tab stop, arrow keys move the choice, and no tooltip anywhere (the accessible name carries what the icon means, and hover does not exist on a phone). `system` is a RULE, not a colour: it resolves to light or dark and keeps resolving, so the distinction lives in WHICH button is marked, and — for a reader who cannot see the mark — in the half-disc's name, which appends what it currently resolves to. Plain DOM and inline currentColor SVG, sized in em: the fleet's two consumers render nothing alike.

variants.description: Pinned to dark — the same colour as system-resolved-to-dark, a different mark.
At phone width, where the 44px target and the absent tooltip matter.
